parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
For 150 randomly chosen trees from this forest, how many would you expect to be classified as
small? 
Trees from this forest are classified as tall if their height is at least h m. 25% of the trees are classified
as tall.

text: The heights of trees in a certain forest are classified as tall, medium or small. The heights can be
modelled by a normal distribution with mean 20 m and standard deviation 5 m. Trees with a height of
less than 14 m are classified as small.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Use an approximation to find the probability that fewer than 27 pupils have music lessons. 
A random sample of 10 pupils from this school is now chosen.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Find the probability that no more than 2 pupils have music lessons.

text: In a certain large school, on average, two pupils in five have music lessons.
A random sample of 80 pupils from this school is chosen.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Draw a tree diagram to illustrate this information, showing all the probabilities.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Find the probability that a randomly chosen student who applies to Drydale College is accepted.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Find the probability that a randomly chosen student who applies to Drydale College takes at least
two tests given that the student is accepted. 
Three friends apply to Drydale College.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text: Find the probability that all three are rejected.

text: Students applying to Drydale College take an entrance test. A student is either accepted or rejected
or required to take another test with probabilities 0.3, 0.2 and 0.5 respectively. When a student takes
a second test the outcomes and probabilities are exactly the same as for the first test. A student who
has to take a third test is accepted with probability 0.25 and rejected with probability 0.75.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Represent this information in a back-to-back stem-and-leaf diagram with Smarts on the left-hand
side. 
For the Teasers, the values of the lower quartile, median and upper quartile are 18, 25 and 37 minutes
respectively.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: On a single diagram draw box-and-whisker plots for the two teams.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Make two comparisons between the times for the two teams.

text: The Smarts and the Teasers are two quiz teams that each contain 11 members. Both complete a puzzle
and the following table gives the times taken, in minutes, by the members of each team.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Find the probability that, on a particular Monday, the team consists of 1 man and 3 women. 
Every Tuesday, the darts club chooses 3 teams of 4. Each team enters a competition in a different
town.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: In how many different ways can the teams be chosen if there are no restrictions?

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
In how many different ways can the teams be chosen if each team must contain at least 1 man
and at least 1 woman? 
The 7 men stand in a line for a photograph. Two of them are brothers, George and Harry.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text:
How many different arrangements are there of the 7 men in which there are exactly 2 men between
George and Harry?
